{
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "confidence": 0.5,
  "anomalies": [
    {
      "category": "polarity",
      "components": ["Q1", "U6"],
      "pins": ["Q1.2", "Q1.3", "U6.1", "U6.6"],
      "nets": ["+5V", "USBC_VBUS_IN"],
      "observed": "The USB input PMOS Q1 (AO3401A) has its source (S, pin 2) on the +5V net and its drain (D, pin 3) on USBC_VBUS_IN. LTC4412 U6 VIN (pin 1) is on USBC_VBUS_IN and SENSE (pin 6) is on +5V. The body diode of Q1 therefore conducts from +5V toward VBUS when the FET is off.",
      "expected": "For reverse-current protection on the USB input, the PMOS source should be on the input (VBUS) and its drain on the system +5V, so the body diode blocks current flowing back into the USB input. The other PMOS load switches (Q6, Q9) use the source-on-input, drain-on-load pattern.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"Q1\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"S\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"Q1\") (pin \"3\") (pinfunction \"D\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"U6\") (pin \"1\") (pinfunction \"VIN\") (pintype \"power_in\"))"},
        {"source": "spec", "quote": "need reverse current protection mostly"}
      ],
      "impact": "The OR-ing/ideal-diode path does not block reverse current from the +5V rail back into the USB input, so the intended protection fails and the USB input path can be back-fed.",
      "confidence": 0.4
    },
    {
      "category": "wrong_value",
      "components": ["R36"],
      "pins": ["R36.1", "R36.2"],
      "nets": ["VOUTN", "VOUTP"],
      "observed": "R36 is annotated with value \"24k\" (and is simulated as 24k), but its MPN (FRC0805J240TSD, '240' code) and its description (\"...24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor\") both indicate a 24 Ω part.",
      "expected": "The schematic value should match the orderable part: a 24 Ω part if that is what is fitted, or a 24 kΩ part with a matching MPN and description if that was intended.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R36\") (value \"24k\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(field (name \"MPN\") \"FRC0805J240TSD\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R36 VOUTN VOUTP 24k"}
      ],
      "impact": "If a 24 Ω resistor is fitted across the VOUTP–VOUTN output, it would load the supply heavily and could overheat or fail. If 24 kΩ was intended, the BOM would be ordering the wrong part.",
      "confidence": 0.35
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The netlist shows the USB input PMOS Q1 with source and drain reversed relative to the other PMOS switches and the LTC4412 reverse-current intent, and R36 is annotated 24k while its MPN and description specify 24Ω. Both are plausible deviations but neither is conclusively proven from the files, so confidence is moderate."
}

anomalies.observed: The USB input PMOS Q1 (AO3401A) has its source (S, pin 2) on the +5V net and its drain (D, pin 3) on USBC_VBUS_IN. LTC4412 U6 VIN (pin 1) is on USBC_VBUS_IN and SENSE (pin 6) is on +5V. The body diode of Q1 therefore conducts from +5V toward VBUS when the FET is off.
anomalies.expected: For reverse-current protection on the USB input, the PMOS source should be on the input (VBUS) and its drain on the system +5V, so the body diode blocks current flowing back into the USB input. The other PMOS load switches (Q6, Q9) use the source-on-input, drain-on-load pattern.
anomalies.impact: The OR-ing/ideal-diode path does not block reverse current from the +5V rail back into the USB input, so the intended protection fails and the USB input path can be back-fed.

anomalies.observed: R36 is annotated with value "24k" (and is simulated as 24k), but its MPN (FRC0805J240TSD, '240' code) and its description ("...24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor") both indicate a 24 Ω part.
anomalies.expected: The schematic value should match the orderable part: a 24 Ω part if that is what is fitted, or a 24 kΩ part with a matching MPN and description if that was intended.
anomalies.impact: If a 24 Ω resistor is fitted across the VOUTP–VOUTN output, it would load the supply heavily and could overheat or fail. If 24 kΩ was intended, the BOM would be ordering the wrong part.
